---
title: "MAF-dependent effect scaling with maf_effect_s"
format:
  html:
    toc: true
---

`maf_effect_s` is an optional effect-variance scaling policy. It is independent
of the public `s` model prefix: `sbayesc`, `sbayesr`, and `sbayesrc` mean
summary-statistics data, not an active MAF scale.

For allele frequency (p_j), let

$$
h_j=2p_j(1-p_j),\qquad q_j(S)=h_j^{S+1}.
$$

- `maf_effect_s = NULL`: no MAF-dependent scale is requested;
- a finite scalar: use fixed (q_j(S));
- `maf_effect_s = -1`: explicitly request the scale while obtaining
  (q_j(-1)=1), the unit-scale numerical reduction;
- `estimate_maf_effect_s = TRUE`: sample supported scalar-trait S parameters.

BayesC-like active-effect variance is multiplied by (q_j(S)). BayesR and
BayesRC multiply their component-scaled covariance by (q_j(S)). The component
multiplier and MAF scale remain separate metadata. Sampled MT `maf_effect_s` is
explicitly unsupported; supply a fixed scalar or `NULL`.

Prior initialization includes these marker scales. Fixed `maf_effect_s` uses
its resolved scale vector; sampled scalar models use `maf_effect_s_init` for
the one-time calibration. `B` is not dynamically renormalized as sampled
`maf_effect_s` changes during MCMC.

## Frequency provenance

Use `effect_maf` to provide an explicitly aligned population frequency when
available. Otherwise the resolver prefers GWAS-summary frequency, then
analysis-genotype frequency by construction. Reference-panel MAF for external
summary statistics is not silently presented as GWAS-population MAF; it
requires `allow_reference_maf_for_maf_effect_s = TRUE`.

Fits record `effect_maf_source`, population, alignment status, and whether
fallback was used. Marker IDs, alleles, frequency population, and effect scale
must all match. Packed-BED routes use the selected analysis-genotype
frequencies unless an explicit aligned `effect_maf` is supplied.

MAF or heterozygosity annotations may coexist with `maf_effect_s`, but the fit
records this overlap because component-probability and variance-scaling effects
may be confounded.

See the [selection-S workflow](https://github.com/psoerensen/sblr/blob/master/examples/workflows/maf_effect_s_workflow.R)
and the [model contract](../dev/blr_model_contracts.md).
